questions.question: Why is `if seen.get(target - x):` a bug in pair search?

options.b: Index 0 is falsy, so a valid match at index 0 is ignored

questions.explain: Test with `is not None` or membership; 0 is a legitimate index.

questions.question: What should the map store to answer "where did this value first appear?"
questions.section: Deep dive: collisions, ties, and what the map represents
questions.explain: Store exactly the information the question needs; a set or count loses the position.

questions.question: Expected time of the hash-map pair search on n integers?
questions.explain: n iterations, each with expected O(1) lookups and inserts.

questions.question: Grouping anagrams of n words of length k by sorted letters costs about…
questions.explain: Each word's key costs a sort of k letters.

questions.question: Why can the left pointer move right when the sum is too small (sorted input)?

options.a: nums[left] plus any remaining right value is at most the current sum, so it can't reach target

questions.section: Deep dive: the geometry of pointer movement
questions.explain: Every partner of nums[left] that remains is ≤ nums[right], so nums[left] is eliminated.

questions.question: Two pointers on an unsorted list for pair sum…
questions.explain: The elimination argument needs sorted order.

questions.question: Time of an opposite-end two-pointer scan?
questions.explain: The gap shrinks by one each step: at most n−1 moves.

questions.question: Stable compaction with read/write pointers keeps…

options.a: the relative order of kept elements

questions.section: Stable compaction is a different invariant
questions.explain: Kept elements are written in the order they are read.

questions.question: Which input breaks a checker that returns True after the loop without checking the stack?
questions.explain: Unclosed openers remain on the stack; the answer must be `not stack`.

questions.question: In a next-greater scan, why store indexes instead of values?

options.b: The answer must be written to the waiting element's position

questions.section: Monotonic stacks store indices, not just values
questions.explain: The index says where the answer goes, and distinguishes equal values.

questions.question: Total time of the monotonic-stack next-greater algorithm?

options.a: O(n²) because of the inner while

questions.explain: Each index is pushed once and popped at most once.

questions.question: Why prefer an explicit stack over recursion for deeply nested input in Python?

options.a: The recursion limit (about 1000 frames) can be exceeded

questions.explain: An explicit list grows on the heap and isn't limited by the interpreter's call depth.

questions.question: With half-open bounds `lo, hi = 0, len(nums)`, what does `while lo < hi` stop with?
questions.explain: The answer range [lo, hi] shrinks to a single point.

questions.question: Why does a prefix-sum array start with 0?

options.a: So a range starting at index 0 is prefix[j] − prefix[0]

questions.section: Why prefix sums need an initial zero
questions.explain: prefix[k] is the sum of the first k values; the empty prefix has sum 0.

questions.question: Kadane's `running` holds…

options.b: the best sum of a subarray ending at the current index
options.c: the sum of all values so far

questions.section: DP as a recurrence, not a table
questions.explain: best is the global maximum; running is the state 'ending here'.

questions.question: Binary search requires…

options.b: a predicate that is monotone over the search space

questions.explain: False…false, true…true (or the reverse) is what lets you discard half.

questions.question: Two pointers that only move toward each other inside one while loop run…
questions.explain: Each iteration moves one pointer; there are at most n moves in total.

questions.question: Binary search on n items takes about how many comparisons?
questions.explain: Each comparison halves the candidates.

questions.question: What does `nums.pop(0)` cost on a Python list of length n?
questions.explain: Every remaining element shifts one place; use deque.popleft().

questions.question: Merge sort's recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + Θ(n) solves to…
questions.explain: log n levels, Θ(n) merging per level.

questions.question: Inserting at the front of a Python list of length n costs…
questions.explain: Every existing reference shifts one slot.

questions.question: What is the invariant of stable zero compaction?

options.a: nums[:write] holds the non-zeros seen so far, in order

questions.explain: That prefix is exactly the answer for the processed part.

questions.question: Rotating [1,2,3,4,5] right by 7 gives…
questions.explain: 7 mod 5 = 2, so the last two elements move to the front.

questions.question: Why fill sorted squares from the right?

options.a: The largest square comes from one of the two ends

questions.explain: The extreme magnitudes are at the ends; the smallest may be anywhere in the middle.

questions.question: Which three things must every recursive function have?

options.a: A loop, a stack and a return
options.b: A base case, progress toward it, and a correct combination
options.c: Memoisation, a cache and a limit

questions.explain: Induction then proves it correct.

questions.question: Why is naive recursive Fibonacci exponential?

options.b: The same subproblems are recomputed many times

questions.explain: Memoisation computes each fib(k) once.

questions.question: In subset backtracking, what does `chosen.pop()` do?

options.b: Restores the state expected by the sibling branch

questions.explain: Every change made before a recursive call is undone after it.

questions.question: Recording `output.append(chosen)` without copying gives…

options.b: Many references to the same list, all equal at the end

questions.explain: Lists are mutable references; copy when you record.

questions.question: Reversing a list, what must you save before `current.next = previous`?
questions.explain: Once overwritten, the unsaved continuation is unreachable.

questions.question: Why use a dummy head?

options.b: So deleting or inserting at the front needs no special case

questions.explain: Every real node then has a predecessor.

questions.question: Why do slow and fast pointers meet inside a cycle?

options.a: Fast closes the gap by one node per step

questions.explain: Modulo the cycle length, the distance shrinks by one each step.

questions.question: Accessing the i-th node of a linked list costs…
questions.explain: You must follow i links from the head.

questions.question: Why use `deque.popleft()` instead of `list.pop(0)` for a queue?
questions.explain: deque supports O(1) operations at both ends.

questions.question: BFS gives shortest paths when…

options.b: every edge has the same weight
options.c: the graph is a tree only

questions.explain: Nodes leave the queue in nondecreasing distance.

questions.question: When should BFS mark a node as seen?
questions.explain: Marking on discovery prevents queueing the same node twice.

questions.question: Why does the window-maximum deque hold indexes?

options.a: Indexes say when an element expires and distinguish equal values

questions.explain: Expiry depends on position, not value.

questions.question: A stable sort guarantees that…

options.a: equal keys keep their input order

questions.explain: Python's sort is stable, which makes multi-pass sorting work.

questions.question: Using `<` instead of `<=` when merging makes merge sort…
questions.explain: On ties the right element would jump ahead of the left one.

questions.question: Counting sort on n values in the range 0..K costs…
questions.explain: It never compares elements, so the comparison lower bound doesn't apply.

questions.question: To sort by count descending, then name ascending, use the key…
questions.explain: Negating the count flips its order while names stay ascending.

questions.question: XOR of all values finds the singleton only if…

options.a: every other value appears exactly twice (an even number of times)

questions.explain: Pairs cancel; three copies would not.

questions.question: What does `x & (x - 1)` do?
questions.explain: Subtracting 1 flips the lowest set bit and the zeros below it.

questions.question: Python's `2**31 + 2**31` overflows to a negative number?
questions.explain: Simulate fixed width with masks when a problem requires it.

questions.question: Why does the sum formula fail if the input may contain duplicates?

options.b: Its precondition (all distinct, exactly one missing) no longer holds

questions.explain: An algorithm's preconditions are part of its correctness.

questions.question: What is a brute-force oracle for?

options.b: Checking a faster solution on small inputs

questions.explain: Obvious-but-slow code is a trustworthy reference.

questions.question: Kadane initialised with best = 0 fails on…
questions.explain: The answer must be a non-empty subarray; for all-negative input it's negative.

questions.question: A solution returns the right pair in the wrong order. That's a…
questions.explain: The algorithm may be fine; the output contract isn't met.

questions.question: Random differential testing compares…

options.a: two runs of the same function
options.b: the fast solution with an independent oracle on many random inputs

questions.explain: Disagreement pinpoints a failing input to debug.
